# NOTES: "Missing: A Romance" by Julius Chambers (1896), Gutenberg #74830

Single book, no separate volumes.

## FRAME / PREFACE
- Sargasso Sea: within a week's sail of New York; ~200,000 sq mi (about Texas); 22°–28°N, 25°–60°W. Called "Harbor of Missing Ships." Narrator's signature: J. C.

## CH I: A Knight-Errant of the Sea
- Narrator: Capt. Austin Clark, American, born/raised Brooklyn. Apprenticed on "Black Ball" line NY–Liverpool. Then Cameron & Co., second mate at 23, four voyages round Horn to Melbourne, became first mate; at 27 commanded ship 3 months after captain's accident.
- Offered captaincy of tramp steamer **Caribas** (named for Marquis of that name), sent by **Triplett & Jones**, Plymouth. Ship in Erie Basin, NY. Mahogany cabin; hardwood forecastle.
- Crew of forty; posted "Missing" at Lloyds NY & London for two years.

## CH II: My Fatal Curiosity
- Sailed from Harbeck's Stores, NY, June; bound Azores: Horta, Ponte Delgada, then Lisbon for orders.
- Passenger **Arthur Gray**, claims to be artist; portfolio. Has Secor launch (direct-explosion engine, extra shear).
- Day 3: at Gray's urging altered course; after longitude 40 steered SE; day 5 sighted derelicts.
- Mirage in eastern sky: ships in orderly arrangement (the "City of Ships"). Lookout reported moving objects.
- Narrator launches in Secor launch with quadrant, chronometer, provisions; first mate left in charge. Second mate wanted to come; refused.
- Launch: Narrator at tiller, Gray at engine. Canal width ~Grand Canal Venice. Narrator felt seasick from swell under sod.

## CH III: I Am Betrayed
- Gray took repeating rifle (Winchester) to bow, pretext of shooting wild fowl. Gray guided with landmarks (redwood tree, logwood trunk, wire grass, sunken tree).
- People on hulks; Gray says "They are my countrymen!"
- Engine quit (Gray's false adjustment); oars dropped overboard.
- Narrator's revolver had no loaded cartridges. He secretly dropped cartridge belt into sea.
- Landed on hulk (25 ft above water, listing), infested with insects and serpents. Trees from upper Amazon.
- **Kantoon** of the ship (60, grizzly gray beard trimmed to 3 in., porpoise-skin dress, leather cap) stands in a tub of water.
- Narrator's small room: bunk of grass cloth stuffed with seaweed; bolted door; crude carvings on walls.
- Ship's name: **Happy Shark**.

## CH IV: The People of the Sea
- Gray in shark-skin garb. Admits he's a "child of this people": ill with smallpox, set adrift by captain of schooner from Bermuda to Canaries; rescued by Sargassons.
- Gray: crew to be given choice to assist navigation or "extinction." Chief Kantoon dwells on ship far in interior; inland sea like Japan's; "Grand Kantoon who rules the sea and air."
- Gray had been allowed to revisit US after oath.
- Narrator: "Flatbush English" rebuke. Locked up at night.

## CH V: Sargasson Manners and Customs
- Morning coffee of brown decoction from leaves/twigs of parasitic plant.
- Murder punished by drowning in barrel. Narrator may not show anger.
- Kantoon stands in barrel of water. Polyglot speech (Spanish, German, French, Italian). Narrator compares to Salvini's Hamlet.
- History: Sargassons date 300+ years, from Spanish Armada galleons; later African slave-ship mutineers (early 1800s) swelled population.
- Ships last ~50 years. When ship sinks, Kantoon calls death chant. Children who rebel are lashed; fettered prisoners starve or are fed to sharks.
- Narrator overhears plot: Caribas to be seized that night.
- Bolt on outside; Narrator locked in. Clouds, mist.

## CH VI: Attack on the Caribas
- Red light in south: **Sacred Fire** (locomotive headlight with magnifying glass, placed over embers in iron hulk; reflected off clouds).
- Priest of Sacred Fire gives life as bond. Fire kept only on iron hulk.
- Unknown woman left wicker dish of boiled seaweed and biscuits at door each night.
- Water from rain; distilled from locomotive boiler ship.
- Day 5: Kantoon with bleeding head wound tells attack story. Boats: grass matting, fish-scale gum, tennis-bat paddles.
- Attack: Chief Kantoon's orders; Gray guided, guarded by two men with instructions to drown him if treacherous. Fifty miles in ~8 hours. 200 attackers. Tabasco-like powder in fish bladder plus opium-like fungus drug.
- Winchester in attackers' hands with ~6 cartridges.
- Attack timed at seven bells ("All is well").

## CH VII: The Agony of Suspense
- Kantoon narrates: boatswain (sturdy, rugged) had seen Sacred Light; refused by first mate; roused the watch, sounded alarm whistle. Crew fought; boatswain chopped cables.
- Cabin boy (sweet-faced, begged life) followed second mate over side, tied and weighted.
- Crew knocked with marlin spikes, thrown overboard.
- Boatswain: lashed to davit; asked sparing of cabin boy. Chose drowning in water cask; held by six men.
- Caribas steam banked; boilers raised by daylight; Kantoon gives narrator binoculars.
- Narrator's jewelry, books, glasses kept in trust.
- Narrator despairs.

## CH VIII: Fidette
- Young woman, hazel-brown eyes, reddish-brown hair, speaks Creole French. Brings rhododendron (affection) and wicker tray of berries. Says "Come, I will take you where we may see the sun go down."
- Captives isolated five days.
- **Fidette's mother** (Marie, New Orleans creole, convent-educated, eloped with gambler son of sugar planter/brigadier-general). Went to Saratoga 1872 aboard small steamer to New York; storm; mother left alone on abandoned ship. Ship was **George Cornwall**, Capt. Timothy Rogers, lost from New Orleans.
- Kantoon of Happy Shark chose her as prize; married by Deputy Chief Kantoon.
- Narrator kisses Fidette.

## CH IX: An Old Man's Darling
- Kantoon angry: Narrator "made eyes" at "little Shark"; threatens separation: Caribas to become his cantonment; narrator to be executive of Happy Shark. Narrator defends.
- Kantoon's story of wife; Fidette born ~2 years after marriage. Chief Kantoon stood godfather; christened by Priest of Sacred Fire.
- Kantoon cannot read; mother educated Fidette in French.
- Ship population: 85 people.
- Government notes: Kantoon's authority; first mate maintains moisture against dry rot; drinking water as intoxicant; seaweed pudding; fish; Ogalla berry.
- Punishment for wife-abuse: wife executed.
- Death ritual: hands and feet drawn backward into "D" shape; kissed; tossed in sea. Heaven: warm three-foot-deep water.
- Sinking bark with barnacles left to die.

## CH X: Cooking for All
- Morning swim: Fidette dives from stateroom window into sod-lined tank; narrator guards with spear.
- Trip to Cook-ship (floating kitchen) with ten boats, provisions requisition on tarpon scale. Rainwater awning. Cook-ship produces dried fish and farina.
- Passed the Caribas in new slip; Caribas moored to stumps and trees.
- Barnacle soup.

## CH XI: "Music Hath Charms"
- Fidette and narrator on bowsprit. Fidette's first love: **Don Fernandez Otranto** (son of exiled Portuguese marshal, Azores penal servitude); played trombone. Met on ship **Royal George** (ex-Sir John Franklin ship; rechristened **Goo-ge-Goo** or **Green Octopod**). Sprig of bay exchanged. Humpbacked daughter of that Kantoon informed on them; ship sank; Fidette believed all lost.
- Sudden trombone sound from west: Portuguese national hymn. Fernandez alive.

## CH XII: Agony of a Jealous Heart
- Narrator jealous; "I always disliked the trombone." Fidette: must not meet until "Week of Silence" ends; will dance Bamboola with Fernandez.

## CH XIII: "The Week of Silence"
- Sun Dance ("Glorification of the Sun"), 3 a.m. wake; seaweed sleep week; "Dance of the Derelicts" (Fidette's hornpipe, Kantoon and first mate). Fidette ate ravenously.
- Trombone heard again at midwatch. Fidette at cabin window. "There was murder in my heart."

## CH XIV: The Kantoon's Displeasure
- Visitors' day. Fernandez arrives without fish scale; Fidette douses him with bucket of water. Kantoon sends men; Fernandez stepped into sack and drowned.
- Fidette sits with narrator on bowsprit afterward.

## CH XV: The Chin-Goone Revolt
- Engagement recognized. "Month of the Visitation": women gossip. Ladies' gifts: sprig of myrtle, shark vertebra. Two fair Greek girls.
- Rumors that Fidette is a vampire. Kantoon: rebellion from Fernandez's former crew, 12 other crews. Chin-Goone history (scuttled 100 ships in 1816 Napoleon/St Helena plot).
- Narrator recalls USS Wabash, Virginius troubles.

## CH XVI: The Papier-Mâché Oranges
- Fidette's basket of Wilmington, Del. fireworks (bombs) found in a box of wreckage. Narrator recalls explosion at Brandywine Creek factory.
- Narrator warns Fidette: radius 25 ft. "Blood oranges."
- Rebel leader **Hansko Yap**, sentenced to death for being half inch short of six feet. Foremast of his ship, 80-foot tapered spar capped with iron, used as battering ram by 40 swimmers.

## CH XVII: The Spar Fight
- Narrator on morning watch sees spar approach. Sargasson swimmers kill sharks with knives. Rope fender stops first two blows.
- Boats (20) capsized; crew killed; boarding party swarm; Kantoon killed (slashed calves by Lascar).

## CH XVIII: Fruit for Dead Men
- Fidette climbs rigging with wicker basket of bombs; throws four onto enemies; blows up the boarding party. "Fidette had recaptured the ship!"

## CH XIX: Fidette Becomes Mine
- Six escaped under spar. Kantoon's body placed in cabin; funeral next day, sewn in tarpaulin, weighted by last anchor.
- Civil marriage at mainmast; narrator and Fidette wed. Fidette's promise: never mention trombone man.
- Baptism with rain water.

## CH XX: Making New Boats
- Narrator's regret about Caribas; "I was the most miserable of men."
- Narrator accused of treachery; ships' fate. Boats made from roots and fish-scale gum. Diver deaths. Ceylon grapevine telegraph (sea-root cables transmit sound).
- Narrator cooks chowder at night, fire forbidden on ships.

## CH XXI: I Become a Sargasson
- Galley **Unk-ta-hee** (60 ft, 30 paddlers) from High Priest of Sacred Fire. Trip to floating monastery in Inland Sea. Compass swings four points. Golden tableware, orange-hued wine.

## CH XXII: A Solemn Ceremonial
- Chief Kantoon; High Priest of Sacred Fire in black chasuble. Oath with white-hot marlinspike touches each shoulder.
- Chief gives narrator the Caribas: "Possess it, if necessary, at the point of the knife." Old commander (Gray) must destroy himself.

## CH XXIII: The New Life
- Full moon worship. Walrus-skin coat. Barge returns; Caribas seen at 12 o'clock. Ship's bridge officer; prize crew with tarpon scale.
- In after-cabin: **Arthur Gray** tied in chair.

## CH XXIV: The Last of an Enemy
- Gray tied in "drowning chair." Gray: "You never can effect your escape from the Sargasso Sea!" Scuttled Secor launch.
- Barge commander: "Basta! You stoppa too longa." Gray drowned: "Let him walk with God!"
- First mate retained as executive. Blood stain on deck. Fidette's cabin adjoins narrator's.

## CH XXV: The Danger of an Idea
- Donna Elenora (wife of Kantoon of ship **Cormorant**) and Fidette start women's reform. Narrator, a supporter of women's rights, encourages. Fidette's mandolin song (Wurra, wurra, wink-o-chee).
- Narrator's cousin in Brooklyn "Amazons" club.

## CH XXVI: The New Woman in Sargasso
- Gig given to women. Cormorant's Kantoon locks wife in sick bay. Fidette: "We'll crucify such a man."
- Teas with hot fire; covetousness; ogalla-berry rouge.
- Sacred Light announces theft of the **Sacred Flint** — flashed.

## CH XXVII: Even in Sargasso Doth Envy Find a Place
- First mate: thief burned, eyes plucked, roasted. Elenora borrowed flint via Chief Kantoon's daughter. Fidette confesses tea was hot.
- Narrator sends boatloads of flint ballast; men carry flints; Sacred Fire reassured.

## CH XXVIII: Plotting Treason
- Fidette helps retrieve engine parts. Narrator plans escape; boatswain recruited. Oil from porpoises.
- Women cook with barnacle-salt smoke disguise. Eight-man cabins locked with padlocks (gross). Sailor missing.

## CH XXIX: The Caribas Under Steam
- Knife grinder (old scissors-grinder) sings Knife-Grinder's Song. Weapons collected.
- Boiler fired at night with boatswain; steam to 85–115 lb. Narrator plans to kill furnace men if failed.
- Acid in cylinder frees piston.

## CH XXX: Farewell to the Floating Continent
- Steam; anchor chain cut; bow to westward. Sacred Fire: "The Caribas is gone! Her Kantoon shall die. A Kantoonship to his captor!"
- Rams Unk-ta-hee barge; 30 men killed.
- Fuel exhausted after two days steaming north; four days drifting; German steamer **Nordland** (from Gibraltar to NY) gives aid; six days to New York, anchored in the Horseshoe.
- Telegram from Triplett & Jones: "Proceed Santos, then Buenos Ayres for orders."
